hypothesis: Preserving effective scope policy across native tool-control routing lets the existing unsupported-option boundary reject native launches before process creation whenever the adapter cannot enforce KOTA scope policy, without exposing hosted-only named tool callbacks to the native loop.

metricsCompared.name: restrictive scope-policy cases reaching native process launch
metricsCompared.baseline: 5 representative write, network, module, and confirmation policies were stripped before native adapter preflight
metricsCompared.candidate: 0 of 5 representative policies reached the native adapter runner

metricsCompared.name: focused harness and workflow regressions
metricsCompared.baseline: the workflow capability regression expected resolved scope policy to be absent from native launches
metricsCompared.candidate: 73 focused tests passed across shared routing, workflow execution, delegation, handoff, and all native adapter declarations

metricsCompared.name: workflow-critical validation
metricsCompared.baseline: no fail-closed coverage for native workflow scope-policy routing
metricsCompared.candidate: 396 workflow-critical tests plus type checking and production build passed

metricsCompared.name: post-check failure reproduction
metricsCompared.baseline: the broad repair check timed out type checking and reported 15 failures across six test files
metricsCompared.candidate: type checking and all 216 tests in the six reported failure files passed when run without broad-suite resource contention

metricsCompared.name: direct workflow-context native policy enforcement
metricsCompared.baseline: direct ctx.runAgentHarness calls omitted effective scope authority for native harnesses
metricsCompared.candidate: 0 of 2 direct native launches reached the adapter under write-disabled and network-denied policies; 13 focused tests and type checking passed
metricsCompared.unit: native runner invocations and static gates

rationale: This repairs a confirmed high-severity authorization bypass at both agent-step and direct workflow-context dispatch boundaries. Native adapters still omit hosted-only named tool controls, but effective scope policy can no longer disappear before capability enforcement. Real native adapters declare scopePolicy unsupported, so affected workflow launches fail before hooks or process creation, and focused plus workflow-critical validation passes.
